title: Access control
notes: Authentication establishes identity; authorization determines allowed operations. An Access Group selects application access and roles. RBAC assigns capabilities through roles, Access of Role to Object rules and privileges. Hiding a button alone is not server authorization.

Dependent roles reuse standard permissions while allowing targeted overrides. Parent-class permissions can be inherited by child classes. Inspect explicit grants/denials and dependent-role order; do not treat permission inheritance as an unconditional union of all permissions.

Attachment categories organize documents and restrict attachment actions through privileges, When conditions and applicable team constraints. All configured When conditions must be true; at least one required privilege must be held. Use When rules for category conditions, not Access When rules.

ABAC supplements RBAC by comparing operator and object attributes for granular access. An Access Control Policy identifies the controlled action; an Access Control Policy Condition expresses the decision logic. Evaluate row and property restrictions in every relevant access path.

CBAC supports client requests to inspect, correct or erase their own personal data through a request-management application and participating repositories. Configure the permitted data and operations; CBAC is not ordinary role authorization or proof of legal compliance by itself.
examples: A service representative can update customer requests, while a supervisor role has a separate approval privilege. Check direct action calls as well as portal visibility.
Start from the standard user role and override only the permission needed for a specialized case class. Test both the explicit override and inherited operations.
Keep incident photos and restricted financial documents in separate categories. Grant read access to the intended role and verify create/edit/delete independently.
Only investigators whose region matches a case may read it. Compare operator region and case region in a policy condition, then apply the read policy.
A customer submits a correction request through the designated request-management flow. Validate identity, locate the configured personal data and apply the permitted correction.
pitfalls: UI visibility
A hidden approval button prevents all unauthorized calls.
Enforce authorization on the server operation.
RBAC versus ABAC
Roles alone express every object-specific attribute condition.
Use ABAC where the decision depends on operator and object attributes.
Category conditions
One true When condition overrides other false conditions.
All category When conditions must be satisfied.
questions: A user has signed in successfully but must not approve refunds. Which concern decides approval access?
Authorization
Authentication alone
The portal's background color
The queue's display name
Authentication confirms identity. Authorization controls allowed actions after identity has been established.
An approval button is hidden for regular users. Which additional control is necessary?
A server-enforced role or privilege check on approval
Only a smaller icon
Only a tooltip
No further check because hidden UI is sufficient
Direct requests can bypass presentation. Authorization must protect the operation itself.
A custom user role needs one exception while retaining standard capabilities. Which approach supports maintainability?
Use a dependent standard role with a targeted override
Copy every permission into unrelated roles indefinitely
Grant all developer privileges
Remove all class inheritance
Dependent roles reuse common permissions and let the application customize only the difference.
An attachment category has two When conditions and a required privilege. One When condition is false. May the user perform the action solely because they hold the privilege?
No; all configured When conditions must also be true
Yes; privileges bypass category conditions
Yes; attachments have no access control
Only the file extension decides
Category authorization combines the required privilege and condition constraints. A false required condition blocks the action.
A team needs different access for photographs and salary documents attached to cases. Which mechanism fits?
Separate attachment categories with appropriate privileges and conditions
A higher assignment urgency for salary files
A new ruleset patch for every file
One public URL with no controls
Categories organize attachment types and provide category-level action restrictions.
Access should depend on whether a case's classification is within the operator's clearance. Which model fits?
ABAC with a policy and policy condition
Authentication alone
A static portal title
A field-value translation alone
ABAC compares object attributes with user attributes, enabling granular access beyond membership in a role.
Which TWO responsibilities are separated in ABAC configuration?
A policy identifies the controlled action
A policy condition evaluates relevant attributes
A theme decides server access
A work queue replaces identity verification
Policy and policy condition separate the protected action from the comparison logic used to decide access.
Customers need a configured workflow to request corrections to their own stored personal data. Which mechanism is most directly relevant?
Client-based access control
Role-based access control alone
Field-level auditing alone
An attachment category alone
CBAC provides a framework for client personal-data requests. It still requires identity and operation-specific configuration.
A dependent-role list contains different explicit decisions for one class. Which detail must be reviewed?
The dependent-role order and the application's explicit overrides
Only the most permissive decision anywhere in the list
Only the operator's division
Only the portal the user opens
Dependent-role evaluation is not an unconditional union of all grants. Order and explicit permissions affect the result.
Does implementing a personal-data request framework alone prove that every regulatory requirement is satisfied?
No; the framework must be configured and evaluated against the actual requirements
Yes; configuring CBAC certifies the whole application
Yes; CBAC eliminates retention policies
Yes; client requests never need identity checks
CBAC supports a class of personal-data operations. Broader obligations and operation-specific safeguards still require evaluation.

title: Securing and auditing data
notes: Encryption protects sensitive persisted data using managed cryptographic keys. Individual properties and BLOB data can have different encryption configurations; consider exposed columns as well as serialized data. Password hashing is a different, irreversible mechanism. Encryption does not replace authorization or safe key handling.

Standard case history records actions; field-level auditing records configured field changes, including old/new values, actor and time. Enable auditing for relevant fields and inspect embedded data fields when needed. Auditing is evidence after a change, not a mechanism that blocks the change.
examples: Protect a sensitive account field and review its exposed-column storage as well as the case BLOB. Manage keys securely and verify that only authorized paths can obtain readable data.
Audit a dispatch address so investigators can see who changed it and when. Keep access to the audit record appropriate because it can contain previous sensitive values.
pitfalls: Hash versus encryption
A password hash is decrypted to authenticate a user.
Hashing is distinct from reversible data encryption.
Audit versus permission
Enabling field auditing prevents unauthorized edits.
Use authorization for prevention and auditing for traceability.
questions: An encrypted case BLOB is introduced. Why should exposed sensitive columns still be reviewed?
They may store values outside that serialized BLOB
All exposed columns cease to exist automatically
Encryption grants every user access
A BLOB is only a browser cache
Protect the actual storage locations. BLOB encryption is not a blanket proof that every separately exposed value is protected.
Which statement correctly distinguishes password hashing from encryption?
Hashing is irreversible; encryption is designed to be reversible with appropriate keys
Every hash is decrypted using the username
Encryption has no keys
Both are only display masks
The two mechanisms serve different requirements. Password verification does not require recovering a plaintext password.
Which TWO concerns remain after sensitive data is encrypted?
Who is authorized to read decrypted values
How cryptographic keys are managed
A need to publish keys in user logs
A guarantee that all users can read the data
Encryption protects stored representation but key access and application authorization still determine exposure.
A field is visually masked in a portal. Which conclusion is unsafe?
Its persisted database value is necessarily encrypted
The UI hides some displayed characters
Storage configuration should be inspected
Authorization still matters
Presentation masking does not prove encryption at rest. Verify the property and actual persistence configuration.
A team must identify who changed a case's delivery address and its previous value. Which feature fits?
Field-level auditing
Only a portal logo
A connector timeout setting
A ruleset prerequisite
Field-level audit entries capture actor, time and changed values for configured fields.
Which TWO are expected in a field-change audit record?
Old and new field values
Who made the change and when
A guarantee that the change was correct
The browser's theme color
Audit records provide traceability. They do not establish business correctness merely because an action was recorded.
Standard case history records routing and status changes. What should be configured to track a specific embedded field?
Field-level auditing for the relevant embedded field
Nothing; every property is audited by default
Only the assignment deadline
A new mock exam
Detailed field auditing is configured explicitly; general case action history is not the same as a full record of every property edit.
Does field-level auditing prevent an unauthorized user from changing a value?
No; permissions must prevent unauthorized changes
Yes; auditing replaces all roles
Yes; audit dates lock the case permanently
Only if the new value is shorter
Auditing records changes. Authorization is the preventive control.

title: Define run-time settings
notes: Application Settings externalize environment-dependent values such as endpoint addresses and resource settings. Configure typed settings and useful categories, reference them from integrations, and resolve the appropriate environment values at runtime. Avoid hard-coded QA URLs in migrated rules; settings are configuration, not permission to expose secrets.
examples: A shipping connector uses an endpoint setting with separate Development, Staging and Production values. After migration, verify both the selected environment and the resolved address using a synthetic test request.
pitfalls: Migration equals configuration
Exporting a connector changes its hard-coded URL automatically.
Reference environment-aware settings and validate them on the target.
Settings versus credentials
Put every credential in a public setting label.
Use appropriate protected authentication configuration.
questions: An integration has different URLs in QA and Production. Which design avoids changing its rule for every deployment?
Reference an Application Setting with environment-specific values
Hard-code the QA URL permanently
Change the case urgency on release
Copy a new connector for every operator
Application Settings centralize values that vary by environment rather than requiring rule edits for each promotion.
After promotion, calls still go to QA. Which check is most direct?
Inspect the resolved environment setting and connector reference
Check only the portal icon
Increase the SLA goal
Reset every user's worklist
The reference and selected environment determine the endpoint. Visual or routing changes do not correct it.
Which TWO are useful properties of Application Settings design?
A value type appropriate to the resource
Categories that group related settings
Unrestricted publication of secrets
A new case type for every address
Types help represent values correctly; categories help find and maintain related settings.
Several integrations share an external host. What is an advantage of referencing configuration rather than literals?
The relevant environment value can be maintained centrally
Calls no longer need authentication
External systems cannot fail
The setting creates all SOAP mappings automatically
Configuration reduces scattered edits. It does not remove authentication, failure handling or data mapping.
Which task validates an added integration resource setting?
Resolve it in the target environment and test a safe request
Look only at its category name
Assume export changes every URL
Hide all error logs
A setting's presence does not prove correct resolution or connectivity in the target environment.
A resource setting contains a port number. Which design principle applies?
Use the supported value type matching the resource rather than an unrelated value
Always use a case's status as the port
Derive the port from urgency
Create a ruleset for each digit
Typed settings express the resource configuration clearly and avoid unrelated business fields.
Why should a setting reference be used instead of a hard-coded server name in a migrated rule?
The server name can differ between environments
Rules cannot contain strings
Work queues are always environment-independent
Settings automatically grant admin access
Environment-dependent resource addresses are the core motivation. Settings do not grant administrative rights.
An endpoint is configured correctly. What requirement still needs separate configuration?
Authentication to the external service
A new browser theme for every call
A ruleset skim after each request
A new operator for each response field
An address establishes where to call; authentication establishes the permitted caller. They are separate integration concerns.

title: Activities and Automations
notes: Activities run ordered steps for procedural processing. Prefer a suitable out-of-the-box automation, Data Transform or specialized rule before custom activity code. Activities increase maintenance cost; a requirement for an activity should be explicit rather than a default for every data update.

An activity step specifies a method, parameters and optional step page. The step page supplies the data context; Pages & Classes declares page/class references. Preconditions, loops and transitions control execution. Call returns to the caller; Branch transfers execution without returning to subsequent caller steps.

Declare OnChange watches configured property changes and can execute activities or suspend work through a business-exception condition. Its trigger is a change, unlike a Declare Expression's derived-value dependency. Keep frequently triggered processing small and guard it with suitable conditions.
examples: Use a Data Transform for a simple address mapping. Use an appropriate standard automation for a supported case action; justify any custom activity with a missing specialized mechanism.

An activity loops through embedded Item pages, setting the step page to the current item. A Call to validation returns for later processing; a Branch is appropriate only when the caller must not resume.

When a RiskScore changes above a threshold, an OnChange condition triggers the appropriate investigation activity. Test repeated changes and ensure the activity does not create an unintended change loop.
pitfalls: Activity by default
Use custom activities for every mapping and calculation.
Evaluate specialized and declarative rules first.
Call versus Branch
Both continue at the next caller step.
Call returns; Branch does not resume the caller sequence.
questions: A requirement only copies and maps fields between pages. Which mechanism should be evaluated before a custom activity?
Data Transform
A new Java activity for every property
A Product rule
A Work Group
Data Transforms specialize in data manipulation and avoid unnecessary procedural maintenance.
A standard case automation already satisfies a requirement. Which design choice is preferred?
Use the supported automation instead of duplicating it in custom code
Rewrite all of its behavior in Java
Remove all case steps
Hard-code it into a portal label
Reusing supported automation reduces custom behavior to maintain and upgrade.
An activity step must operate on an embedded item page. Which field sets that context?
Step page
Only the ruleset version
Only the operator timezone
The exam domain
The step page determines the page against which the method runs. Declare its page/class context appropriately.
An activity invokes another activity and must continue with its next step afterward. Which instruction fits?
Call
Branch
Stop all processing
Split Join
Call returns control to the caller; Branch transfers processing without continuing the caller's subsequent sequence.
Which TWO are part of an activity step's execution definition?
A method and its parameters
A step page when a different data context is required
Only a portal logo
A certification pass mark
Methods, parameters and page context define the procedural operation and where it acts.
A property change should trigger an activity when a business condition becomes true. Which rule fits?
Declare OnChange
A Product rule
A Field Value used only as a label
A work queue name
Declare OnChange monitors property changes and invokes conditional processing.
Why should a frequently changing watched property be considered carefully?
The triggered activity can add repeated processing cost
OnChange never executes more than once
It automatically caches every connector response
It replaces every access role
Frequent triggers can cause significant overhead. Scope and guard the processing appropriately.
A total should stay derived from component amounts without an action side effect. Which rule better matches than OnChange activity code?
Declare Expression
An attachment category
A Product rule
An operator record
A derived value is a declarative dependency. OnChange is for actions tied to change, not a default replacement for expressions.

title: Background processing
notes: Queue processors handle queued items asynchronously; job schedulers wake on a schedule to run an activity. Queue individual work with Run in Background or Queue-For-Processing. Schedule recurring scans with a job scheduler. Neither choice removes the need for safe retries and observable failure behavior.

Queue processors manage their processing transactions; avoid adding conflicting object-save/commit steps to their activity. Job scheduler activities manage the read/write work they perform. Investigate broken items and repair the underlying cause before reprocessing; design external effects so retries do not duplicate them.

Node classification assigns runtime work to suitable node types. Separate background workloads from web-user workloads where appropriate; moving work to another node does not fix inefficient code or eliminate shared database contention.

Admin Studio exposes runtime management for queue processors, jobs, nodes, requestors and listeners. Use it to inspect health, failure counts and running resources. A configured but disabled processor is not evidence that queued work is being completed.
examples: After a document is submitted, queue its processing so the interactive case can continue. A nightly reconciliation that discovers records to process is a scheduled job.

A delivery notification may be retried after failure. Use a business identifier to prevent duplicate external notifications, and inspect broken queue items instead of repeatedly replaying a malformed request.
Assign heavy batch jobs to background nodes while keeping web requests on their designated nodes. Recheck database load and user response times after the separation.
In Admin Studio, inspect a processor's broken items and last failure, fix the cause, then use the supported reprocessing operation and verify completion.
pitfalls: Event versus schedule
Use a nightly scheduler for every newly submitted item.
Choose item-driven queueing or time-driven scheduling according to the trigger.
Async equals success
An item was queued, so the external action succeeded.
Observe completion and failure separately from submission.
questions: Each submitted document needs independent asynchronous processing. Which mechanism fits?
Queue processor
Only a nightly job that cannot accept items
A Field Value
A portal theme
Queue processors handle individual queued tasks. A job scheduler is appropriate for a time-driven recurring activity.
A cleanup activity must scan expired records at 02:00 each day. Which mechanism fits?
Job scheduler
A queue processor with no queued items or scheduling logic
Assignment Ready
A case status label
The trigger is a schedule and the activity discovers records to process. That fits a job scheduler.
Which TWO can enqueue a task for background processing?
Run in Background automation
Queue-For-Processing method
Only a Field Value rule
Only a Work Group label
These are supported queue-submission mechanisms; enumeration and team records do not enqueue work.
Why should a queue processor activity avoid adding its own conflicting object commit steps?
The queue processor manages processing transactions
Queue processors never update data
All activities must be read-only
Admin Studio forbids activities
The framework manages transaction boundaries for queue item processing. Duplicating that work can undermine the intended transaction lifecycle.
An item repeatedly fails because its payload is malformed. What is the appropriate next action?
Investigate and correct the cause before reprocessing
Replay it indefinitely with no change
Delete all work queues
Report the item as completed
Reprocessing does not repair bad input. Correct the underlying defect and then verify the retry outcome.
Heavy background jobs interfere with interactive users. Which configuration can separate their application-node processing?
Appropriate node classification for background and web-user workloads
Only a new case label
The same task on every node without classification
A larger urgency increment
Node classification routes workload types to suitable nodes. It does not remove a shared database bottleneck, which still needs measurement.
Where can an administrator inspect queue processors and scheduled jobs at runtime?
Admin Studio
Only the quiz page
Only the property local list
Only the Product rule preview
Admin Studio provides runtime resource and background-processing management.
An item appears in a queue but the processor is disabled. What must not be claimed?
That submission proves successful processing
That the processor's state needs inspection
That queued and completed are distinct states
That runtime health matters
Queue submission acknowledges accepted work, not completed execution. Runtime monitoring must verify the outcome.
